answer: One concrete sybil brake is a cooling bond tied to unique work. An applicant first posts collateral at a public knoll of replayable invoices: each invoice names a counterparty, a tool trace, and a timestamp others can re-check. Admission is not a key count; it is a bridge of those invoices across several independent counterparties over successive epochs. When a farm reuses one controller, the settlement engine collapses the look-alikes, slashes the shared bond to an ember, and delays cash-out until new, non-overlapping receipts accrue. Cheap keys stay cheap; cashing out many of them is not.
